description: Board approved $528,279 purchase of 1,231 iPads + 1,295 keyboard cases for SY26-27 on March 23, 2026 over a Screen Sense Evanston petition with 1,200+ signatures. Declining the purchase would have produced a one-time savings of $528,279.
notes: ONE-TIME, not annual recurring (shown at full one-time value). Trimmed from the original $551,135 / 1,300-iPad request. The District's existing 4-year operational lease (approved Dec 2024) is $750,966 = ~$200K/year on a separate stream. Annualized over a 5-year iPad lifecycle ≈ ~$106K/year.

measure: Choose lowest bidder for special ed transport (KalaJu over BriteLift)
description: On December 15, 2025 the Board approved a special ed transportation contract with BriteLift in a 6-1 vote (Opdycke opposed). KalaJu Elite Fleet's bid was ~$1M lower at headline ($1,035,232 vs $2,040,896) but only priced 30 of the 55 needed routes.
source: FOIA Gras post 253 (2026-03-07, "kalaju-protest-letter"); D65 Board action 2025-12-15
notes: UNCERTAINTY: KalaJu only priced 30 of 55 routes. CFO Mitchell stated KalaJu's bid was based on their existing fleet capacity, not the 55 routes needed. Tom Hayden's analysis notes nothing in the KalaJu bid stated this limitation. Annual savings range: ~$143K (linear extrapolation of KalaJu's per-route cost across 55 routes) to ~$1M (headline bid difference). Chart shows $1M (the figure as reported by Hayden); description / page text discusses the range.
